script: Who owns what. Many pay problems are handoff problems: each person assumed someone else had it. Here's your part as the HCM, who else acts, and what happens next.
You own the record. You enter hires, changes, and terminations for your area, and you check time cards every week. Payroll can only pay what the record says.
Compensation owns the job behind the pay. They pick the job code and level, and issue the pre-search and reclass memos. Don't decide exempt or non-exempt status yourself.
Recruiting and central HR own moves that come from a requisition. A transfer or promotion that came from a job application is processed by central HR. Don't submit it yourself.
Employees and managers own the hours. The employee approves their time card, the manager approves it, and payroll signs off. You check that nothing is stuck.
Finance partners own the funding. Get the costing string from your finance partner. In many areas, the finance partner also enters costing, so confirm who owns it in your department.
Payroll owns the payroll run, and every correction. Bring payroll the facts: what was expected, what was paid, and what the record shows. Payroll decides how and when to correct the pay.
Track your transaction until it's approved. Check the notifications bell daily, and before the cutoff. A transaction that's still pending doesn't pay.
Two things to remember. Never try to run or rerun payroll yourself. And never create a direct hire for someone already in a recruiting process.
